acceptance: Adaptive query families without title-only false positives

Run contract preflight before release

rules.behavior: Musical-work admission becomes intentionally less strict each manual round: first round requires strong independent matches (three sound evidentiary signals as the working model); second needs two credible matches; third needs one; fourth and later may admit a YouTube result on requested title alone, explicitly accepting possible non-covers. A YouTube video ID/link validity check is separate and NEVER loosened. Strong matches discovered late remain eligible. Do not keep an always-on same-Work gate that silently defeats the later rounds.
acceptance: Round 1 rejects a same-title unrelated 1924 work when seeking a known later work
Round 2 admits candidate with two available musical identity clues without demanding third
Round 3 admits candidate with one clue
Round 4 admits same-title video without documentary authorship/year, without labeling it guaranteed cover
Audio/video technical validity remains unchanged in every round

rules.behavior: Each round adds up to 50 genuine NEW YouTube-linked visible results when available, with no need to fill a quota. Publish each verified video thumbnail immediately, one by one, without waiting for a 5/10/25/50-item batch, a global 5/10-second seal, mandatory first-block gate, or other batch threshold. Preserve existing positions, do not rerank displayed rows, and keep player/UI/audio responsive. Do not invent results.
acceptance: First verified thumbnail appears before the remainder of that round has completed
A second verified thumbnail appends without moving the first
Empty or slow sources do not block a verified video from another source
At most 50 new results per round and no false placeholder

rules.behavior: Only ONE button below the visible results, with two mutually exclusive states: ORANGE 'Completa tornata' while the CURRENT round still has planned searches/pages/verifications that can continue; each press resumes from durable in-session query/page checkpoints under the SAME musical-identity strictness. GREEN 'Cerca ancora' only when the current round's planned work is genuinely exhausted (or its 50-new-video quota reached with no further publication this round), then pressing starts the NEXT less strict round and returns the button to orange. No separate second button, no automatic transition to a lower-precision round, no timeout falsely counted as source exhaustion. Previous thumbnails stay cumulative, immovable, no identical recording/video duplicates.
acceptance: Two states of one button; orange 'Completa tornata' and green 'Cerca ancora'
Repeating orange continues previously unfinished queries/pages and never resets already completed work
An empty batch while unfinished keeps orange; timeout does not falsely mark complete
Green initiates exactly next round with relaxed precision threshold
Already displayed results stable and duplicates excluded through the session

rules.behavior: First round seeks highest-confidence official/released covers, original performer's studio/live/duets, strong documented renditions, and FOREIGN/LANGUAGE-ADAPTED covers from COVER.INFO FROM THE VERY FIRST SEARCH in parallel with YouTube and other useful sources. Exploit existing COVER.INFO YouTube video IDs after technical metadata confirmation rather than rediscovering them. Second round expands to talent, live, acoustic, semi-official; third to independent, amateur, instruments; fourth+ rare/long-tail/title-only. These are preferences, not exclusivity: a strong official match found late is still admitted. Never make SecondHandSongs the main provider. Keep categories Tutto/Studio/Live/Remix/Stranieri without replacing the native categorization system.
acceptance: Foreign COVER.INFO records are considered in round 1, including different-language titles with documentary relation
Pre-linked COVER.INFO YouTube IDs go through lightweight technical verification and correct YouTube thumbnail
Round families expand without disabling high-confidence matches
Fourth round permits title-only candidates
Native five categories remain usable

rules.behavior: All visible ranking/confidence labels on CoverLab cards are a single approximate 0%-100% musical-match precision percentage (e.g. 10%, 70%, 80%, 95%). NEVER display legacy 1..20, 20/20, 10/20, or a raw 0..100 points score as a distinct scale. Percentage is an estimate, NOT a statistical guarantee that the item is a cover; very low precision remains allowed in later rounds. Remove every percentage-based distribution/quota formula between rounds (such as 20% previous, 10% old categories), preserving only the per-card confidence percentage. Legacy numerical fields may remain in archival storage for backward compatibility but cannot override active visible rules.
acceptance: No /20 or /100 point indicators visible on Turbo Cover cards
Cards show percent signs for estimated match precision only
Rounds do not enforce percentage-based source/category quotas
10% candidates are not automatically rejected in later rounds

rules.behavior: CoverLab visible results show ONLY each found YouTube video's authentic thumbnail derived from that video's valid video ID and its corresponding already-identified YouTube link. NO discographic record covers, editorial poster fallback, grey/red provisional nonvideo cards, embedded autoplay video inside scrolling wall, or red/green status dots. On tap pass the SAME video ID to the existing native playback path without re-searching which video matches; stream resolution on playback is allowed. Verify YouTube metadata/availability before first publication to the feasible level, but do not claim metadata check guarantees streaming on every device.
acceptance: Every published visible result has a valid YouTube video ID, thumbnail URL and link bound to the same ID
No catalog-only or poster-first visible path, including Cloud cache/fallbacks and recovered old history
No red or green status dots in Turbo results
Tap never searches for a different video ID; native player receives selected ID
No embedded video surface within the scrolling cards

rules.behavior: Same-session results and cursor are cumulative append-only and previous cards never shift, including while showing details and returning; dedupe exact video ID and identical recording within that active CoverLab visit. When user truly leaves CoverLab and later starts a new visit/search, clear round counters/cursors/temporary exclusions and retry state; no permanent user-wide rejection blacklist. Audio keeps precedence and searching must not cause stutter, ANR or playback interruption.
acceptance: Exiting CoverLab then starting a fresh visit resets temporary rounds/exclusions
Opening details then returning retains active session and scroll position
No persistence of temporary negative matches as a global exclusion list
Playback and scrolling remain responsive while discovery runs

rules.behavior: Before ANY future app implementation, read this canonical behavior contract, old version/history and current code, identify old conflicting enforcement routes, and present the specific old->new conflict and exact protected scope to the user for approval. The new approved requirement replaces contradictory rules in the SAME scope only; retain compatible functioning behavior, exact signing/package ID, native player, graphics outside requested button/dot/score changes, LAST_GOOD, main/MADRE/production, and free-only dependencies. Do not assert implemented before device/end-to-end test; static tests and compiled APK alone cannot prove search quality.
acceptance: Pre-change report identifies conflicts and protected components before writing app code
Negative tests prove poster-first/batch-first/strict-work-after-round3 and old scores no longer run after implementation
Live sample search verifies quick YouTube thumbnail publication, categories, progressive manual turns and playback
No protected production/MADRE/player regression
